bottom_line: LCZ696 versus enalapril reduced the primary composite of cardiovascular death or first heart-failure hospitalization (hazard ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.73 to 0.87).
implications: In this trial, compared with enalapril, LCZ696 was associated with lower event rates for the primary composite (21.8% vs. 26.5%; hazard ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.73–0.87), cardiovascular death (13.3% vs. 16.5%; hazard ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.71–0.89), and death from any cause (17.0% vs. 19.8%; hazard ratio 0.84, 95% CI 0.76–0.93). The data also show more symptomatic hypotension with LCZ696 (14.0% vs. 9.2%) alongside less cough (11.3% vs. 14.3%) and fewer creatinine elevations ≥2.5 mg/dl (3.3% vs. 4.5%). These numbers support a conclusion of superiority for the prespecified outcomes in this studied population and do not, by themselves, establish effects in populations not meeting the trial’s entry/run-in requirements.

major_points.text: Primary composite outcome was lower with LCZ696 vs enalapril.
major_points.quote: the primary outcome had occurred in 914 patients (21.8%) in the LCZ696 group and 1117 patients (26.5%) in the enalapril group (hazard ratio in the LCZ696 group, 0.80; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 0.87; P<0.001)

major_points.text: Cardiovascular mortality was lower with LCZ696 vs enalapril.
major_points.quote: of these patients, 558 (13.3%) and 693 (16.5%), respectively, died from cardiovascular causes (hazard ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.71 to 0.89; P<0.001)

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was lower with LCZ696 vs enalapril.
major_points.quote: A total of 711 patients (17.0%) receiving LCZ696 and 835 patients (19.8%) receiving enalapril died (hazard ratio for death from any cause, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.76 to 0.93; P<0.001)

major_points.text: First hospitalization for worsening heart failure was lower with LCZ696 vs enalapril.
major_points.quote: First hospitalization for worsening heart failure        537 (12.8)                 658 (15.6)    0.79 (0.71–0.89)        <0.001

major_points.text: Trial was stopped early after crossing a prespecified boundary for overwhelming benefit.
major_points.quote: The trial was stopped early, according to prespecified rules, after a median follow-up of 27 months, because the boundary for an overwhelming benefit with LCZ696 had been crossed.

major_points.text: Safety trade-offs: LCZ696 had more symptomatic hypotension but less cough and fewer creatinine elevations ≥2.5 mg/dl.

inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligibility requirements at screening included an age of at least 18 years

inclusion_criteria.text: NYHA class II, III, or IV symptoms at screening.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligibility requirements at screening included an age of at least 18 years, New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II, III, or IV symptoms

inclusion_criteria.text: Ejection fraction of 40% or less (later amended to 35% or less).
inclusion_criteria.quote: an ejection fraction of 40% or less (which was changed to 35% or less by an amendment to the protocol on December 15, 2010)

inclusion_criteria.text: BNP ≥150 pg/ml or NT-proBNP ≥600 pg/ml, or lower thresholds if hospitalized for heart failure within previous 12 months.
inclusion_criteria.quote: have a plasma B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) level of at least 150 pg per milliliter (or an N-terminal pro-BNP [NT-proBNP] level ≥600 pg per milliliter) or, if they had been hospitalized for heart failure within the previous 12 months, a BNP of at least 100 pg per milliliter

inclusion_criteria.text: Stable beta-blocker and ACE inhibitor (or ARB) dose equivalent to at least 10 mg enalapril daily for at least 4 weeks before screening.
inclusion_criteria.quote: for at least 4 weeks before screening, patients were required to take a stable dose of a beta-blocker and an ACE inhibitor (or ARB) equivalent to at least 10 mg of enalapril daily.

exclusion_criteria.text: Estimated GFR below 30 ml/min/1.73 m2 at screening or randomization.
exclusion_criteria.quote: an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) below 30 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area at screening or at randomization

exclusion_criteria.text: Serum potassium >5.2 mmol/L at screening or >5.4 mmol/L at randomization.
exclusion_criteria.quote: a serum potassium level of more than 5.2 mmol per liter at screening (or above 5.4 mmol per liter at randomization)

exclusion_criteria.text: History of angioedema or unacceptable side effects during receipt of ACE inhibitors or ARBs.
exclusion_criteria.quote: history of angioedema or unacceptable side effects during receipt of ACE inhibitors or ARBs.

criticisms.text: The trial’s comparison was preceded by sequential single-blind run-in periods to ensure acceptable side-effect profile at target doses.
criticisms.quote: a single-blind run-in period during which all patients received enalapril, which was followed by a single-blind run-in period during which all patients received LCZ696, to ensure an acceptable side-effect profile of the study drugs at target doses

criticisms.text: Patients not taking protocol-required ACE inhibitor/ARB at screening (and those taking both) occurred.
criticisms.quote: At the screening visit, 20 patients were not receiving the protocol-required treatment with an angiotensin-converting–enzyme (ACE) inhibitor or an angiotensin-receptor blocker (ARB), and 45 patients were taking both drugs.
